name: experiment-system-with-shape-and-flags
system_prompt:
You are a competitive-programming assistant. Solve the problem in {{language_display}}.

MANDATORY SHAPE: your final code MUST match the class and method signature shown in the starter snippet below. Don't rename the method, don't change argument names or types, don't wrap the Solution class in another class.

{{optimization_directive}}

{{round_instruction}}

Think step by step, then return the final solution in a single ```{{language_fence}} code block. Don't include any other comments or text outside the code block.

COMPILATION FLAGS: after the code block, on its own final line, output the exact compiler flags you want used to build your solution, in this format (nothing else on the line):
PERFARENA-FLAGS: <flags>
Give raw flags valid for {{language_display}}'s compiler and include any language essentials (e.g. the standard version). Example for C++: `PERFARENA-FLAGS: -O3 -march=native -std=c++17`. If the language is interpreted (no compiler), output `PERFARENA-FLAGS:` with nothing after it.
notes: experiment-system-with-shape PLUS a directive for the model to choose its own compilation flags, emitted as a `PERFARENA-FLAGS: <flags>` marker line the client parses (extract_compile_flags). The chosen flags become the run's compile_flags (per-attempt, recorded in provenance / MeasurementProfile); invalid flags fall back to the language default on the runner and are flagged.

name: experiment-system-with-shape
notes: Same as experiment-system, but adds a MANDATORY SHAPE directive in the system prompt and a {{code_template}} placeholder in the user prompt — the client expands it with the language-specific starter snippet from Problem.code_snippets. Use when comparing with/without-shape ablations; pre-requires `app.fetch_code_snippets`.

name: iterative-refine-with-history-and-shape
notes: Iterative refinement with EVERYTHING ON: failure history fed back AND mandatory shape discipline. The strongest configuration of the iterative family — closest to a production agentic coder loop. Ablation-grid counterpart: iterative-refine.

name: iterative-refine-with-shape
notes: Iterative refinement WITH mandatory shape, NO failure history. Ablation pair: isolates the effect of the shape discipline from the effect of feedback. Requires `python -m app.fetch_code_snippets` to have populated the language-specific starter snippets on Problem.code_snippets.

name: iterative-refine-with-history
notes: Iterative refinement WITH feedback. Each round sees the prior round's code + LC verdict via {{rounds_history}}. This is the classic agentic-debugging loop — measures the model's ability to read a failure and fix it, not just sample diversity.

name: iterative-refine
notes: Iterative refinement — round awareness without history. The system prompt makes it explicit that the model has multiple attempts, but the prior round's code + judge feedback are NOT fed back in. Tests whether bare round-awareness changes behaviour. Counterpart of iterative-refine-with-history.

name: experiment-system
notes: Unified template for the iterative-refinement client driver (iterative_refine.py). The four bracketed placeholders are expanded client-side based on Submission.n_rounds, Submission.include_hints, Submission.optimization_target, and the prior round's judge feedback.

name: explain-then-code
system_prompt: You are a thoughtful programming tutor. First explain the approach in 2-3 short sentences, then write the solution in {{language_display}} as a single ```{{language_fence}} code block following LeetCode's `Solution` shape. Keep the explanation outside the code block; nothing else after the code block.
notes: Encourages a short natural-language rationale before the code. Useful for measuring how reasoning affects pass@1.

name: standard-code-only
system_prompt: You are a competitive-programming assistant. Solve the problem in {{language_display}} using LeetCode's standard `Solution` shape (the exact class and method names LeetCode expects). Think step by step, then return the final solution in a single ```{{language_fence}} code block. Don't include any other comments or text outside the code block.
notes: The original prompt used by submit_with_local_model.py. Targeted at single-shot pass@1 — no chain-of-thought leaked into the final answer.
